findings.text: STEP sets the surface on the neighbouring English word in a few verses: Mic 7:17 gives H7264 "turn" and H6342 "come trembling"; Gen 27:33 gives H2731 "said"; Psa 14:5 and 53:5 give H6343 "great"; Job 3:25 gives H6343 "thing". The face was read from the verse, not from the surface word.

Face A, felt before a threat or a person: trembled, trembling, afraid, fear, anguish, shuddering and panic, with an army, an enemy's anger, a prophet's arrival, the multitude, the oppressor or a discovery as the object.

Face B, felt before God's presence, act or word, or a spirit: dread, terrified, trembled and trembling, with God's presence, his voice in the thunder, his word read aloud, a vision or his act as the object; once a spirit in the night.
Face C, spoken against: "Do not be in dread", with a ground; self-spoken "I will not be afraid".
Face D, fearing or trembling before God as a standing: trembling at his word; "let him be your dread"; fearing "always"; awe of his words.
Face F, what or who inspires dread: God named "the Fear of Isaac"; a person who is an object of dread; Ephraim's speech.
Face G, dread laid on nations and peoples: laid by God, or fallen on peoples because of Israel, the Jews, Mordecai, a king.
Face I, not fearing: no fear of God; not afraid at his word; not trembling before a man; creatures without fear.
Face J, other: "no hands were wrung for her" (Lam 4:6).
Face K, terror that comes upon: terror as an event that falls, strikes, overwhelms, comes like a storm; terror, pit and snare; a trembling heart given in the curse.
Face L, none to make afraid, and its inversion: promised peace, "none shall make you afraid"; the same phrase used of corpses no one drives the birds from, and of deserted cities.
Face M, making others afraid, as an act: the subject is the one who frightens (a counsellor, a judge, sorceries, debtors, God's messengers, "horns").
Face N, the earth, heavens, waters and the dead tremble: the subject is the physical world, or the dead, before God.
Face O, *rāgaz* stirred: one root rendered rage, anger, quarrel, grief and disturbance; the subjects include God, Sennacherib, David, Joseph's brothers, a fool, Samuel brought up and Sheol.
Face P, trembling as care, concern or a start: trembling for someone or something, or a sudden start.
Face Q, coming to God in trembling: movement toward God, trembling.
Face R, trembling joined with joy or good: the dread root rendered "thrill"; trembling "because of all the good".
Face S, trembling of the body in age: "the keepers of the house tremble".
Face T, trembling called for: a summons or decree to the earth, the peoples, the complacent and the heavens.

Dread and trembling arise before God's presence, voice, word and act: "I am terrified at his presence; when I consider, I am in dread of him" (Job 23:15-16); "At this also my heart trembles" at the thunder (Job 37:1); "all the people in the camp trembled" at Sinai (Exo 19:16); at Daniel's vision "I stood up trembling" (Dan 10:7, 10-11); "they turned trembling to one another, saying, 'What is this that God has done to us?'" (Gen 42:28); "The sinners in Zion are afraid" (Isa 33:14); "I was in terror of calamity from God" (Job 31:23); "Will not his majesty terrify you" (Job 13:11).

Trembling comes at an arrival or a discovery: the elders "came to meet him trembling" (1Sa 16:4); Ahimelech "came to meet David, trembling" (1Sa 21:1); "all the guests of Adonijah trembled" (1Ki 1:49); Isaac "trembled very violently" (Gen 27:33); "the man was startled" (Rut 3:8); "all the people followed him trembling" (1Sa 13:7); "Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled" (Isa 10:29).

God lays dread on peoples, and the verses say what follows: "The Lord your God will lay the fear of you and the dread of you on all the land" (Deu 11:25); "the Lord brought the fear of him upon all nations" (1Ch 14:17); "the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms" and "they made no war against Jehoshaphat" (2Ch 17:10); "Terror and dread fall upon them ... they are still as a stone" (Exo 15:14-16); "dread of them had fallen upon [Egypt]" (Psa 105:38); "Trembling took hold of them there" (Psa 48:5-6); "that the nations might tremble at your presence" (Isa 64:2).

Making others afraid, as an act (the subject is the one who frightens): Ahithophel, "throw him into a panic" (2Sa 17:2); Gideon "threw all the army into a panic" (Jdg 8:12); to Babylon, "perhaps you may inspire terror" (Isa 47:12); "so that man who is of the earth may strike terror no more" (Psa 10:18); "those awake who will make you tremble" (Hab 2:7); "Will you frighten a driven leaf" (Job 13:25); "to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations" (Zec 1:21); "messengers ... to terrify the unsuspecting people of Cush" (Eze 30:9).

"Do not be in dread" comes with its ground: "for the Lord your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God" (Deu 7:21); "for it is the Lord your God who goes with you" (Deu 31:6); "for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go" (Jos 1:9); "Fear not, nor be afraid; have I not told you from of old" (Isa 44:8); self-spoken, "I will trust, and will not be afraid" (Isa 12:2) and "whom shall I fear?" (Psa 27:1).

findings.text: "None shall make you afraid" is the promise of peace: "you shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid" (Lev 26:6); "no one shall make them afraid" (Mic 4:4); "none shall make them afraid" (Zep 3:13); "with none to make them afraid" (Eze 39:26; 34:28); "none shall make him afraid" (Jer 30:10; 46:27); "be disturbed no more" (2Sa 7:10); "He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid" (Psa 78:53); "none will make you afraid" (Job 11:19).

The dread root appears in joy: "your heart shall thrill and exult" (the paḥad verb, "to dread", H6342) (Isa 60:5); "They shall fear and tremble because of all the good and all the prosperity I provide for it", after "I will forgive all the guilt of their sin" (Jer 33:8-9); with "rejoice with trembling" (Psa 2:11).

findings.text: Trembling is called for and decreed: "tremble before him, all the earth!" (Psa 96:9; 1Ch 16:30); "let the peoples tremble!" (Psa 99:1); "Tremble, O earth, at the presence of the Lord" (Psa 114:7); "Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble" (Joe 2:1); "Tremble, you women who are at ease" (Isa 32:9-11); Darius, "people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel" (Dan 6:26); "Be appalled, O heavens" (Jer 2:12).

The earth, mountains, heavens, waters and the dead tremble, with the words used of people: "the whole mountain trembled greatly" (Exo 19:18); "the foundations also of the mountains trembled and quaked" (Psa 18:7); "the deep trembled" (Psa 77:16, 18); "who looks on the earth and it trembles" (Psa 104:32); "The pillars of heaven tremble" (Job 26:11); "The dead tremble under the waters" (Job 26:5); "I will make the heavens tremble" (Isa 13:13); "the mountains quaked" (Isa 5:25); "The earth quakes before them; the heavens tremble" (Joe 2:10); "Shall not the land tremble on this account" (Amo 8:8); "Under three things the earth trembles" (Pro 30:21-23); also 1Sa 14:15, Isa 23:11, Hab 3:7.

One root, rāgaz, "to tremble", is rendered by the ESV as trembling and quaking (Exo 15:14; Psa 18:7; Hab 3:16), "Be angry" (Psa 4:4), "raging" and "raged" (2Ki 19:27-28; Isa 37:28-29), "enraged" (Eze 16:43), "provoke" (Job 12:6), "quarrel" (Gen 45:24), "rages" (Pro 29:9), "deeply moved" (2Sa 18:33), "disturbed" (1Sa 28:15), "stirred up" (Isa 14:9), "roused" (Isa 28:21), "unrest" (Jer 50:34).
